senses.definition: To make something hard to understand on purpose.
senses.caution: This is an allegation of bad faith, not a comment on clarity. Aimed at a vendor's pricing page it is fair game; aimed at a colleague's slide it says they meant to mislead, and the room will hear that even if you did not mean it. If all you mean is that the explanation came out muddled, say obscure or unclear and keep the temperature down.
senses.example: Their per-token pricing obfuscates the real cost, so I have rebuilt it as one number per thousand queries.

cues.text: A vendor's pricing page looks designed so that you cannot work out what you would actually pay, and you want the word that says the confusion is the point.
In a review you want to name what a paper is doing when it buries a bad number under three layers of terminology.
You are arguing that adding yet more caveats to the report would hide the finding rather than qualify it.
A friend's phone contract seems written so the exit fee is impossible to find, and you want the accusing word for it.
Talking about an interview where a politician used a great many words to avoid a plain yes or no.

distractors: To check a claim against its source.
To repeat a point until it lands.
To explain something clearly enough for a beginner.
To shorten a document without losing its meaning.
To translate a technical answer into business terms.
